title: Epistaxis and nasal packing
stem: ENT room. Mr Lui, 68, on apixaban for AF, has had a left nosebleed for 40 minutes despite pinching. HR 96, BP 168/94. Manage the bleed and pack the nose on the model.

phases.title: Assess
phases.goal: First aid, his circulation, the anticoagulant, and a look inside.

phases.title: Cautery
phases.goal: A visible anterior point: cautery, safely.

phases.title: Pack
phases.goal: Still bleeding: an anterior pack, correctly.

phases.title: Refer
phases.goal: ENT, the anticoagulant, and what if it is posterior.

notes:
Checked against the ENT UK/ British Rhinological Society epistaxis guideline (2017 consensus) and NICE CKS.

First aid: sit up, lean forward, firm pressure on the soft part of the nose for 10–15 minutes, ice to the mouth; assess ABC and haemodynamics, check anticoagulants and bloods (FBC; clotting if on warfarin). Examine with a headlight and speculum after suction; apply topical vasoconstrictor/anaesthetic (co-phenylcaine). If a bleeding point is seen anteriorly (Little's area): silver nitrate cautery (one side of the septum only, 10 seconds, not on active bleeding). If not controlled: anterior packing (nasal tampon such as Merocel or Rapid Rhino inserted along the floor of the nose, parallel to the hard palate) and ENT referral. Posterior bleed (continuing bleeding into the pharynx despite anterior packing): Foley catheter (12–14 F) passed to the nasopharynx, inflated with water and pulled forward, plus anterior packing; admit under ENT. Tranexamic acid (topical or oral) may be used. Anticoagulants: withhold with specialist input, do not routinely reverse unless life-threatening. Do not pack with a suspected base-of-skull fracture. Antibiotics are not routinely needed for anterior packs.

Your notes match this well (Merocel technique, co-phenylcaine, Foley for posterior bleeds).
